profiles.meeting_scenario: At a large academic hospital, an emergency medicine quality lead and an ED/critical care pharmacy informatics specialist are holding a design review of a revised adult diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) two-bag protocol before it goes to the Pharmacy & Therapeutics committee. The protocol is based on the hospital's 2015 hybrid ED-ICU rollout and is now being adapted for use across the main adult ED. The agenda is to review whether the current order set, protocol language, and implementation notes are ready for broader approval, with attention to feasibility, safety framing, and operational fit. The expected outcome is a shared decision that the protocol is nearly ready for committee submission, with minor edits to wording and workflow instructions.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.role: Emergency Medicine Physician and ED Quality Improvement Lead
members.expertise: Adult DKA management, ED protocol implementation, retrospective outcomes review
members.background: Lena is an attending emergency physician who helped analyze the hospital's before-and-after data on the two-bag method and now chairs the ED protocol revision workgroup.
members.private_state: She wants the review to stay focused on polishing and scaling a protocol she sees as already validated locally, and she wants to avoid reopening foundational debates that could delay committee approval.
hidden_assumptions: "DKA resolution" in this review can be discussed using the same operational milestone emphasized in the local outcomes study, especially first bicarbonate at or above 18 mEq/L.
The design under review is essentially the successful 2015 hybrid ED-ICU protocol, just being cleaned up for broader dissemination rather than materially redefined.
The phrase "adult ED DKA patients" naturally refers to the same practical population used in the original rollout, not every possible adult hyperglycemic admission touching the ED.

"Keeping fluids and electrolytes constant" means both bags are prepared to be interchangeable except for dextrose concentration, so bedside staff can adjust proportions without rethinking the rest of the infusion.

members.name: Aaron Shah, PharmD
members.role: Clinical Pharmacy Specialist in Emergency/Critical Care and EHR Order Set Builder
members.expertise: IV fluid workflows, medication safety, order set standardization, nursing/pharmacy operational design
members.background: Aaron supports ED and ICU medication workflows and is responsible for translating clinical protocols into the live electronic order set and stocking instructions.
members.private_state: He wants the protocol to be executable in every adult ED pod without relying on hybrid-unit staffing patterns or bespoke bag preparation, and he is trying to minimize hidden build complexity.
hidden_assumptions: "DKA resolution" is mainly relevant as the point at which the insulin infusion can be transitioned safely, which requires the usual full transition criteria rather than a single laboratory milestone.
If an order set is labeled for adult ED DKA, it should work across all adult ED starts, including boarding patients and those managed outside the original hybrid area.
"Our two-bag protocol" refers to the currently maintained electronic build and associated pharmacy workflow, not specifically the original pilot-era process conditions.

"Keeping fluids and electrolytes constant" means the bedside workflow should feel stable and standardized, even if the bags are stocked and executed through routine pharmacy/nursing methods rather than perfectly matched interchangeable bags.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the protocol helps patients reach "resolution" sooner and use "resolved" as if it were a shared endpoint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 treats resolution in the review context as the study-style metabolic milestone of first serum bicarbonate at or above 18 mEq/L, which is sufficient to describe protocol benefit and guide pathway wording.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 treats resolution as the practical transition point for stopping the insulin infusion and moving off the pathway, which implies full clinical transition criteria such as gap closure and readiness for subcutaneous insulin.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In DKA discussions, "resolution" is a familiar term and both are speaking positively about earlier improvement, so the word feels safely shared even though one is thinking of an analytic milestone and the other of an operational endpoint.

misalignment_points.topic: Which adult ED patients the review is actually about
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to the design as the protocol for "adult ED DKA patients."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the scope is the practical population represented in the original feasibility experience: adults started under ED-led care in the hybrid ED-ICU style workflow, with familiar exclusions and staffing assumptions in the background.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the scope is any adult patient who enters the adult ED and is placed on the DKA pathway, including boarding patients and non-hybrid pods that need a single standardized order set.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds appropriately broad and professional, and neither person sees a reason to unpack the patient boundary because each assumes the other is simply using a convenient shorthand for the hospital's standard adult ED population.

misalignment_points.topic: Which version of the two-bag protocol they are treating as the reference design
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention "our two-bag protocol" and "the 2015 rollout" as if they are pointing to the same design object.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is mentally referencing the original hybrid-unit protocol as implemented during the local before-and-after evaluation, including the contextual supports that made it feel straightforward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is mentally referencing the current live electronic order set lineage and pharmacy workflow that evolved after 2015, which he sees as the practical version that now defines the protocol.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both versions share the same name, same core concept, and same local history, so the reference sounds identical in conversation even though one person is grounding comments in the pilot-era workflow and the other in the present operational build.

misalignment_points.topic: How 'keeping fluids and electrolytes constant' is supposed to work
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both endorse the two-bag idea because it allows dextrose adjustment while "keeping fluids and electrolytes constant."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes both bags are functionally interchangeable except for dextrose content, so the bedside team can shift the proportions while preserving the same total fluid and electrolyte composition across the pair.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the workflow is acceptable as long as the staff experience a stable overall protocol and standard stocked products can be used, even if electrolyte composition and bag handling are not literally mirrored across both hanging bags at every moment.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase comes directly from how the method is usually summarized, so it feels like settled background knowledge; neither thinks to unpack whether "constant" means chemically matched bags or merely a stable practical workflow.
